page: Amazon Web Services m6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at a speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance provides 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with hyperthreading enabled, yielding 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a score of 2989.08. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling in the bottom 25% with the same score due to the single physical core limitation. Memory performance is generally constrained, with passmark memory scores and cached small-block read bandwidth falling into the bottom 10%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, while complex multi-threaded workloads, such as software compilation and ray tracing, rank in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m6a.large offers a balanced resource profile for entry-level general-purpose workloads without the overhead of high-end compute or memory-optimized hardware. Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and baseline network speed, this instance is suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and single-threaded utility tasks. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded processing, or large-scale LLM inference due to its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks.
